chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū Khālid, the mawlā of ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about one performing a separate ʿumrah: is ṭawāf al-nisāʾ required upon him? He said: ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is not required upon him.

So this does not contradict what we presented earlier, because this report is to be understood as referring to one who entered for a separate ʿumrah during the months of hajj, then wanted to make it into tamattuʿ for hajj; that is permissible for him, and ṭawāf al-nisāʾ does not become binding upon him. This is because ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is only binding on the one performing the separate ʿumrah apart from hajj; when he converts it into tamattuʿ leading to hajj, its obligation falls from him. This indicates that.

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: the months designated for hajj rites
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: the circumambulation specifically required in certain pilgrimage rulings concerning lawful marital relations
key_terms.عُمْرَةً مُفْرَدَةً: an independent ʿumrah performed separately from hajj
key_terms.مُتْعَةً لِلْحَجِّ: tamattuʿ for hajj, where ʿumrah is joined to hajj in the prescribed manner

ai.seo_question: Is ṭawāf al-nisāʾ obligatory in a separate ʿumrah according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling of ṭawāf al-nisāʾ in relation to a separate ʿumrah. The apparent wording is reconciled by explaining that it concerns someone who entered into a separate ʿumrah during the months of hajj and then converted it into tamattuʿ for hajj, in which case ṭawāf al-nisāʾ is not required.
